title: Business Structure Comparison in Nepal: Sole Prop vs. Partnership vs. Pvt Ltd
metaDescription: Compare business structures in Nepal: Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, Private Limited, and Public Limited. Evaluate liability, taxes, and registration authorities.
h1: Business Structure Comparison: Which Factors Should Entrepreneurs Consider?
directAnswer: Choosing a business structure in Nepal depends on three primary factors: personal liability protection, capital requirements, and ownership flexibility. A Sole Proprietorship is simpler to register but exposes personal assets to unlimited liability; a Partnership shares responsibility but retains unlimited liability; while a Private Limited Company (Pvt. Ltd.) registered under Companies Act 2063 provides complete limited liability and scalable corporate shareholding.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.contentHtml:
Carefully evaluate the legal differences between the three most popular commercial entities in Nepal:

FeatureSole Proprietorship FirmPartnership FirmPrivate Limited (Pvt. Ltd.)
Governing LawPrivate Firm Registration Act 2014Partnership Act 2020Companies Act 2063
Registering AuthorityMunicipal Ward Office / Dept of CommerceDepartment of Commerce & SuppliesOffice of Company Registrar (OCR)
Owner LiabilityUnlimited (personal assets at risk)Unlimited (joint and several)Limited strictly to unpaid share capital
Separate Legal Entity?No (owner and firm are one)NoYes (distinct legal person)
Transferability of OwnershipDifficult / Requires firm dissolutionRequires partner consentSimple via OCR share transfer deed (Share Lagat)

For small local retail shops, a sole proprietorship registered at the local Ward Office may suffice. However, for technology startups, trading businesses, consulting firms, or any enterprise seeking bank loans and outside investors, a Private Limited Company is strongly recommended. Discover our specialized business structuring advisory services.

faqs.question: Can a sole proprietorship be converted into a Private Limited company later?
faqs.answer: Yes. A proprietorship can be transitioned into a Private Limited company by establishing a new Pvt Ltd entity and formally transferring assets, liabilities, and trade name through approved board and tax documentation.
